Subject: Sudden throughput drop and 5xx spike — we need immediate assistance

Priya —

We started seeing a sharp throughput drop and rising 5xx rates from ~08:55 PDT. P95 latency jumped from 120ms -> 1.8s for inference and our processing queue backed up. Traffic pattern unchanged on our side; we replayed a sample trace and attached the request-trace-20270417-0910.json plus a snapshot from Grafana (vip_grafana_timeseries_0417.png). Keys:

- Affected routes: /v1/generate (model: open-redwood-13B-fp16) primarily

This is impacting checkout flows. Can we escalate to on-call and get an ETA? We need an exec-level readout if this is going to persist.

Thanks,

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Date: Sat, 17 Apr 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Sudden throughput drop and 5xx spike — we need immediate assistance

Quick triage notes (10:00 PDT):
- Observed: KV cache miss storm concurrent with heavy long-context requests (avg seq len ~1.2k tokens) -> increased memory pressure on a subset of inference hosts.
- Symptom: rapid eviction and rebuild of KV caches caused expensive recompute; kernels got queued leading to timeouts and 5xx propagation (~504).
- Root cause hypothesis: a small percentage of VIPRetail traffic started sending long-context batch requests after yesterday’s model variant rollout; model variant selection routed them to smaller instance profiles.

Actions executed (10:00–10:22):
1) Temporarily enabled model-variant fallback to open-redwood-13B-fp32 on high-latency routes (rolled to 6 nodes) — immediate P95 improved to ~380ms.
2) Increased per-host KV cache size on the affected pool and staged a cache pre-warming job using the sampled prefixes (kv-cache-dump-0417.tar.gz attached).
3) Throttled large-context request concurrency at the edge for VIPRetail to protect latency SLOs while we stabilize.

Next steps (owner / ETA):
- Karthik: deep log correlation and kernel queue profiling — deliverable by 04/18 EOD
- Marcus: orchestration change to pin VIPRetail to the higher-memory instance profile while we complete rollout — target 04/17 14:00 PDT
- Priya: coordinate exec-level note and confirm whether VIP wants a formal readout; Lauren to talk to Tom/Anya on credit/compensation expectations.

We believe the combination of fallback + cache sizing will restore steady-state; will continue monitoring.

— Karthik Iyer
Head of Serving Reliability, Redwood Inference

Anya / Tom —
Quick update from our side after initial mitigations:
- Traffic that hit the problematic path saw P95 drop from 1.8s -> ~420ms after fallback and throttles. 5xxs reduced to ~0.4% across the window.
- We’ve pinned VIPRetail traffic to higher-memory profiles and kicked off cache pre-warm; Marcus confirmed the orchestration change completed at 14:12 PDT.

What we’re proposing next:
1) Formal RCA write-up (Karthik to produce draft) to be delivered by Monday 04/19 EOD.
2) Remediation runbook with short-term config changes + long-term capacity plan (Marcus + infra) — draft by 04/20.
3) Exec readout call w/ VIPRetail leadership and our CTO + Head of Ops — propose Monday 04/19 10:00 PDT (Lauren will coordinate).

We’re also opening a request for goodwill credits for the impacted window; Lauren will lead that discussion. Apologies for the disruption — we’ll prioritize communications and follow-through.

Best,
Priya
